sections.label: Singapore Food Agency and food laws
sections.summary: The Singapore Food Agency was formed in 2019 to consolidate food safety and security functions, and this Bill consolidates relevant food-related laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For more effective governance of food safety and security, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) was formed in 2019 to consolidate these functions under one agency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This Bill serves to consolidate the relevant food-related laws that were enacted at different points in our history.

sections.label: Bill aims and main thrusts
sections.summary: The Bill aims to make food laws simplified, consistent, effective and future-ready, with three main thrusts including consolidating food-related legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: However, our policies must be supported by our laws to enable SFA to achieve its mission of ensuring and securing a supply of safe food in Singapore for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This Bill is timely to bring about several attributes in our laws: simplified, combining elements of the law now scattered in nine Acts to one, reducing complexity and increasing ease of doing business; consistent, bringing several laws that evolved over decades at different times to set common definitions, regulatory regime and penalty framework, thus reducing compliance cost for businesses and increasing the effectiveness of our regulations; effective, enabling SFA to respond quickly and effectively against threats to food safety and security; future-ready, updating our regulations to be relevant for the future, enabling technology and industry practices to innovate and evolve, helping our business grow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: There are three main thrusts in the Bill: first, to consolidate and rationalise food-related legislation; second, to update our food safety regime to better protect consumers, support industry development and prepare for emerging trends; and third, to strengthen our food supply resilience.

sections.label: Offences replaced by Bill part 8
sections.summary: Offences in the Sale of Food Act and other Acts on food sale will be replaced by part 8 of the Bill, covering all food distribution including free food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Accordingly, offences currently in the Sale of Food Act (SOFA) and other Acts that apply to the sale of food will be replaced by part 8 of the Bill, covering all manner of food distribution, including giving food for free.

sections.label: Individual food import allowance
sections.summary: The Bill provides a single rule allowing each individual to bring in not more than 15 kilogrammes of various food categories, including up to 30 eggs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Bill provides a single rule to allow each individual to bring in a total of not more than 15 kilogrammes of various categories of food, including a clutch of up to 30 eggs.

sections.label: New offences for unsafe food
sections.summary: Under the Bill, all food is covered by new offences of supplying unsafe or unsuitable food, regardless of commodity type or business activity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, all food will be covered under the new offences of supplying unsafe or unsuitable food, regardless of the commodity type or business activity.

sections.label: Definition of food handling
sections.summary: Clause 9 of the Bill defines food handling more comprehensively, covering preparation, manufacturing, storing, packing and transporting up to delivery to consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Clause 9 of the Bill therefore defines "food handling" more comprehensively to cover activities from preparation, manufacturing, storing, packing and transporting up to the point of delivery to consumers.

sections.label: Maximum penalties for food safety offences
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to align the maximum penalty for the most serious food safety-related offences to $50,000 for a first-time corporate offender and $25,000 or up to 24 months' jail or both for a first-time individual offender.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to align the maximum penalty for the most serious food safety-related offences to $50,000 for a first-time corporate offender and for a first-time individual offender, to $25,000 or a jail term of up to 24 months or both.

sections.label: Disqualification of ex-licensees
sections.summary: An ex-licensee whose food trading, food business or animal feed production licence has been revoked is disqualified from holding the same licence for up to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under this framework, an ex-licensee whose food trading licence, food business licence or animal feed production licence has been revoked will be disqualified from holding the same licence for a specified period of up to three years.

sections.label: Four new types of directions
sections.summary: Four new types of directions are introduced, and under clause 137 the DG (FA) can issue directions to deal with threats to primary production or food producing animals' health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Four new types of directions are introduced to enable more effective and faster response to food safety threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under clause 137, the DG (FA) will be able to issue directions to deal with threats to primary production or the health of food producing animals to mitigate or prevent a threat to the food supply here.

sections.label: Targeted corrective action directions
sections.summary: Clause 130 will support a more targeted response requiring corrective actions by the individual instead of affecting the entire licensable food business and every other food worker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Clause 130 will support a more targeted response to require corrective actions by the individual, instead of affecting the entire licensable food business and every other food worker of the business in every instance.

sections.label: Appeals, stockholding and farm plans
sections.summary: Existing powers of arrest will no longer be in the Bill; aggrieved parties can appeal to the Minister, and the Bill allows a Minimum Stockholding Requirement and a Farm Management Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Existing powers of arrest, which are provided in current legislation, will no longer be provided in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under Part 12 of the Bill, parties aggrieved by discretionary decisions made by SFA or the DG (FA) can appeal to the Minister, as an independent authority, to reassess the merits of the decision taken.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Two food security measures that the Bill will allow us to implement are: one, a Minimum Stockholding Requirement (MSR) for entities along the food supply chain to hold stocks of essential food items or agri-food production inputs; and two, a Farm Management Plan by local farms to ensure the sustainable scale up of local production.

sections.label: Second reading motion
sections.summary: The question is moved that the Bill be now read a second time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Move the question that the Bill be read a Second time?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I said that I move, “That the Bill be now read a second time.”

sections.label: Agri-food production inputs safety
sections.summary: The Bill contains provisions on two agri-food production inputs, animal feed and plant pesticides, that can affect food safety if not properly used or produced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore contains provisions aimed at two agri-food production inputs which, if not properly used or produced, can directly affect the safety of food produced namely, animal feed and plant pesticides.

sections.label: Animal feed and pesticide regulation
sections.summary: SFA will regulate animal feed for food producing animals and NParks for non-food producing animals, and SFA will regulate pesticides on edible plants while other pesticide use is deregulated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Through amendments in Division 6 of Part 17 of the Bill, SFA will regulate animal feed for food producing animals while the National Parks Board (NParks) will regulate animal feed for non-food producing animals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Through amendments in Division 4 of Part 17 of the Bill, SFA will regulate pesticides use on edible plants while the use of pesticides other than for growing of food will be deregulated.

sections.label: Defined food prior approval
sections.summary: Part 5 of the Bill introduces a category of defined food for food of higher regulatory concern requiring prior approval before supply or advertising in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To achieve this, Part 5 of the Bill will introduce a category of “defined food” to help industry navigate the types of food that are of higher regulatory concern and therefore require prior approval before they can be supplied or advertised in Singapore as food.

sections.label: Untrained food workers offence
sections.summary: Between 2022 and 2024 an average of 43% of food-borne gastroenteritis outbreaks came from poor food safety practices by food workers, and clause 103 makes deploying an untrained food worker an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Between 2022 and 2024, an average of 43% of food-borne gastroenteritis outbreaks resulted from poor food safety practices by food workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Under clause 103, it is an offence if a licensed food business deploys an untrained individual as a food worker in that business.

sections.label: Voluntary recall notification requirement
sections.summary: Industry must inform SFA as soon as practicable or within 24 hours after deciding on a voluntary recall, as when mooncakes with excessive E. coli were found.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In cases of voluntary recalls initiated by the industry due to food safety concerns, the industry will also be required to inform SFA as soon as practicable or within 24 hours after making the decision to recall.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, through SFA’s proactive surveillance, a potential outbreak was averted last September when some mooncakes were found with excessive levels of Escherichia coli, or E. coli.

sections.label: Farm Management Plan requirement
sections.summary: The Farm Management Plan is introduced as a new requirement for licensees undertaking primary production activities, aimed at mitigating food safety and disease risks and ensuring sustainable production.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Currently, all farms are already required to maintain their farms in clean and sanitary conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will strengthen farm management and animal husbandry practices by introducing the Farm Management Plan (FMP) as a new requirement for those licensees undertaking primary production activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The FMP is aimed at mitigating risks to food safety, disease spread and ensuring sustainable production.

sections.label: SFA industry support ACT Fund
sections.summary: SFA will support the industry through practical means, including co-funding technology adoption via the $60 million Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: SFA will continue to support the industry in overcoming challenges through other practical means.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This includes supporting capability development by co-funding the adoption of technology through the $60 million Agri-food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund.

sections.label: MSR in Part 2
sections.summary: The Bill introduces the MSR in Part 2 as another key food security measure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As such, another key food security measure the Bill introduces is the MSR in Part 2 of the Bill.

sections.label: Rice Stockpile Scheme powers to MSE
sections.summary: The Bill right-sites powers to administer the Rice Stockpile Scheme with the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With the Bill, the powers to administer the Rice Stockpile Scheme will be right-sited with the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE).

sections.label: Enforcement actions for non-compliance
sections.summary: The Bill will deter non-compliance through civil and/or criminal penalties, unlike today's only recourse of revoking the rice import licence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Unlike today where the only recourse is to revoke the rice import licence upon non-compliance, the Bill will deter non-compliance through a range of enforcement actions, such as civil and/or criminal penalties.

sections.label: Phased implementation and legislative changes
sections.summary: The Bill will be implemented in phases by 2028, starting with defined foods and non-packaged drinking water in the second half of 2025, with consequential amendments and repeal of SOFA and the Wholesome Meat and Fish Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To support the industry in the transition, the Bill will be implemented in phases by 2028, starting with that for defined foods and non-packaged drinking water in the second half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Second Schedule spells out savings and transitions to ensure a smooth transition to the new regulatory regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will also make consequential amendments to existing legislation that SFA leverages today and repeal and replace the SOFA and the Wholesome Meat and Fish Act.

sections.label: FSSB health promotion regulation powers
sections.summary: FSSB will give the Minister for Health statutory powers to make food-related regulations for health promotion purposes, unlike SOFA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A key difference between SOFA and FSSB is that, FSSB will provide the Minister for Health with statutory powers to make food-related regulations for health promotion purposes.

sections.label: Part 9 food regulations
sections.summary: Clause 174 of the FSSB sets out Part 9 Regulations the Minister for Health may make for health promotion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Under Part 9, clause 174 of the FSSB sets out the types of food regulations, known as Part 9 Regulations, that the Minister for Health is empowered to make for health promotion purposes.

sections.label: More stringent regulations requirements
sections.summary: The Minister for Health must determine an NCD of public health interest and identify the target food when making more stringent regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In making more stringent regulations, the Minister for Health will need to determine a non-communicable disease (NCD) of public health interest and identify the "target food".

sections.label: Enforcement officers remedial notices
sections.summary: Enforcement officers may issue a remedial notice requiring a person to remedy a Part 9 regulation contravention within a specified period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Beyond being provided with investigating powers, enforcement officers may also issue a remedial notice to require a person to remedy a contravention of any Part 9 regulation within a specified period, including directions to take reasonable steps to do so.

sections.label: Safer resilient food system
sections.summary: A safer, more resilient food system supports better population health and nutrition and aligns with preventive care efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A safer and more resilient food system that can also support better population health and nutrition is aligned with our ongoing efforts to strengthen preventive care and will empower Singaporeans to lead healthier lifestyles.

sections.label: Offence supplying expired food
sections.summary: The FSSB makes supplying food past its expiry or best-before date an offence, making some food rescue or donation activities illegal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The FSSB goes further by making it an offence to supply food that is past its expiry or best-before date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What this means is some food rescue or donation activities on the ground will become illegal.

sections.label: Clarify supplying past-date food
sections.summary: The question asks whether supplying food past its labelled date is permissible under any circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether supplying food that is past its labelled date is permissible under any circumstances?

sections.label: Offence of supplying unapproved food
sections.summary: Under Part 5, supplying any defined food without pre-market approval is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under Part 5, it is an offence to supply any defined food without pre-market approval.

sections.label: Clause 20 introduces MSR
sections.summary: Clause 20 introduces the MSR for essential food items like rice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, clause 20 introduces the MSR for essential food items like rice.

sections.label: Personal food import allowance increase
sections.summary: The Bill increases the personal food import allowance to 15 kilogrammes across all categories under clause 44.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill also increases the personal food import allowance to 15 kilogrammes across all categories as stated in clause 44.

sections.label: Surplus food redistribution programme
sections.summary: The programme redistributes surplus food to over 200 residents with student volunteers and is protected by the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our programme, which redistributes surplus food to over 200 residents with the help of student volunteers, thrives under the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act, which protects donors from liability.

sections.label: Tiered penalty framework support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill's tiered penalty framework in clauses 29 to 31 and 144 to 146 for repeat offenders and negligent food handling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the Bill's tiered penalty framework as stated in clauses 29 to 31 and 144 to 146 to address repeat offenders and negligent food handling.

sections.label: Singapore food import dependency statistics
sections.summary: Singapore's food import sources grew from 172 to 180 countries between 2019 and 2021, but five countries supplied about 60% of food in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The number of countries that we import food from grew from 172 to 180 between 2019 and 2021, yet as diversified as our food sources are, according to a World Bank dataset, we remain dependent on a small handful, just five countries, for approximately 60% of our food in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This number has gone up slightly from around 57% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have seen local vegetable and aquaculture farm closures due to unviable economics and the proportional of local vegetables and seafood eaten in Singapore declining since the announcement of the goal decreasing from 4.5% to 3.2%, and 7.9% to 7.3% for vegetable and seafood, respectively, between 2019 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Lastly, in food abundant Singapore, around 10% of Singaporean households are estimated to remain food insecure, primarily due to financial constraints, according to the Hunger Report in 2020, published by the Lien Centre for Social Innovation supported by the Food Bank Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the SFA, in a 2022 food statistics report, we import 90% of our food and 40% of our water, while our local agri-food sector only produces 29% of eggs, 8% of vegetables and 4% of seafood, far from meeting local demand.

sections.label: Urban farm operating costs
sections.summary: Energy, manpower and rent are the largest cost contributors to urban farms in Singapore, with high tech systems being capital and energy intensive.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Energy, manpower and rent are the largest cost contributors to the operation of urban farms in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: High tech farming systems and controlled environment agriculture approaches are capital and energy intensive, while energy price volatility and looming increases in carbon taxes further exacerbates high operating cost concerns.

sections.label: MSR product stock provisions
sections.summary: Part 2 of the Bill lets the Minister specify a food as an MSR product, requiring entities to hold minimum stocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Part 2 of the Bill contains provisions that allow the Minister to specify that a food is an MSR product through subsequent legislation regulations and thus, means that under clause 20, an entity subject to the MSR provisions must hold minimum stocks either on a daily or on average over a period of time, which will be communicated to the MSR entity through a trigger notice under clause 23.

sections.label: Local produce price premium
sections.summary: The average price premium of local produce stands at approximately 30% to 83%.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The average price premium of local produce stands at approximately 30% to 83%.

sections.label: CSA arrangement with schools
sections.summary: A CSA arrangement forms a direct relationship between consumers and farmers, and the member asks about combining central catering and schools with local farms.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under this kind of arrangement, a direct relationship is formed between consumers and farmers, where consumers subscribe to the harvest of a farm or collective of farms, and receive portions of the farms' harvest on a regular basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that we had discussions in this House about the difficulties associated with ensuring that our children and schools are fed well, could we not combine central catering and schools with a CSA type arrangement with local farms in a bid to boost the consumption of local produce?

sections.label: Cost barriers to local produce
sections.summary: Rising cost and the cost premium of fresh local produce stand in the way, hitting low-income households hardest.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Overall, rising cost and the cost premium of fresh local produce are standing in the way, hitting low-income households the hardest.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How can we tackle existing food insecurity and ensure more equitable access to fresh, healthy food for all?

sections.label: Singapore food waste statistics
sections.summary: Food waste accounted for about 11% of total waste generated in Singapore in 2023, with an 18% recycling rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Singapore, food waste accounted for about 11% of the total waste generated in Singapore in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The recycling rate for food waste was 18%, and we can do better.

sections.label: Small community farm licence exemption
sections.summary: Small community farms producing under 200 kilogrammes of food a month need no licence if they avoid pesticides and human, raw animal or bird excreta.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, there is no need for a small community farm producing less than 200 kilogrammes of food a month to apply for a licence if it does not use pesticides or human, raw animal, or bird excreta in the cultivation process.

sections.label: SFA chicken prohibition concerns
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SFA can clarify its concerns and design challenges regarding prohibiting chickens on vegetable gardens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can SFA clarify its concerns and design challenges regarding the prohibition of chickens on vegetable gardens?

sections.label: Victory Gardens production in 1944
sections.summary: By 1944, Victory Gardens produced 40% of all vegetables grown in these countries, freeing packaging and transportation resources and promoting health through physical activity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By 1944, Victory Gardens produced 40% of all vegetables grown in these countries, freeing up resources used in packaging and transportation while promoting better health through physical activity.

sections.label: Evolving SFA beyond regulatory body
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry plans to evolve SFA beyond a regulatory body and hopes SFA lowers barriers for community farming.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask: will there be plans by the Ministry to evolve SFA's role beyond being merely a regulatory body?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we envision an agency that collaborates with citizens – learning together and co-creating solutions for food resilience?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I sincerely hope SFA will work towards lowering barriers for community farming in the spirit of enabling greater citizen participation.

sections.label: 30% local production by 2030
sections.summary: The stated aim was to locally produce 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The stated aim was, I quote, "to locally produce 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030".

sections.label: 30 by 30 aspiration resolve
sections.summary: Koh Poh Koon said the 30 by 30 vision has always been an aspiration, and the speaker hopes this does not imply reduced Government resolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon also said that, and I quote, "the 30 by 30 vision has always been an aspiration." While I note the challenges is mentioned, I do hope that the aspiration will not imply any buckling down from the Government's resolve to achieve its goal of locally producing 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030.

sections.label: Cocoa yields and price rise
sections.summary: Black pod disease and extreme heat followed by heavy rain impacted cocoa yields, raising prices from US$2,500 to US$10,000 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Black pod disease and extreme heat followed by heavy rain impacted cocoa yields, sending price increase from US$2,500 per tonne in March 2023 to US$10,000 a year later.

sections.label: COP29 small states funding
sections.summary: At COP29, many small states were disappointed that they receive US$300 billion instead of the US$1.3 trillion required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In COP29, many small states were disappointed that small states receive much less funding than required – US$300 billion instead of the US$1.3 trillion required.

sections.label: Foods under MSR regime
sections.summary: It asks what other food besides rice will be required to be maintained under the MSR regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Besides rice, which is already subject to the current rice stockpiling scheme, what other food will be required to be maintained under the MSR regime?

sections.label: MSR level for food disruptions
sections.summary: Given Singapore relies on imported food for about 90% of supply, the MSR must sustain the population during significant disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Given that Singapore relies heavily on imported food supply, about 90% of our food supply, the MSR must be set at a level that can sustain our population during significant disruptions.

sections.label: Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund
sections.summary: The $60 million Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund, established in April 2021 by the SFA, supports local food producing companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund is a $60 million fund in Singapore that supports local food producing companies in the agri-food sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Fund was established in April 2021 by the SFA to help local farms adopt advanced farming systems and technology.

sections.label: Developed country agriculture subsidies
sections.summary: The global norm for developed country agriculture policies is direct ongoing subsidies for farms to meet operation expenses tied to various goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The global norm for our agriculture policies in developed country is to provide direct ongoing subsidies for farms to meet operation expenses tied to various goals, such as maintaining soil health, improving livestock management and reducing emissions.

sections.label: SFA support for local produce
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu said SFA supports industry offtake for local produce, including a Government procurement criterion giving points for sustainability initiatives like FTTRP recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Minister Grace Fu, in a recent reply on12 November 2024 to a Parliamentary Question from my colleague, our Aljunied Member, Mr Gerald Giam, shared that the SFA has been supporting the industry in achieving greater offtake for local produce through various initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: She said that this included incorporating a criterion in Government procurement to give additional points to businesses who have undertaken sustainability initiatives, such as being recognised under the FTTRP for procuring locally grown produce.

sections.label: Incentivising institutional buyers for 30 by 30
sections.summary: To support the 30 by 30 goal, efforts should focus on increasing uptake of local food by major institutional buyers through incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Indeed, to support Singapore's 30 by 30 goal of producing 30% of nutritional needs locally by 2030, efforts should focus on increasing uptake of locally produced food by major institutional buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Incentivising these major institutional food buyers through long-term contracts, contractual requirements or price support measures can make locally sourced products more competitive, promoting the market viability of Singapore's local food producers and enhancing national food security.

sections.label: New regulatory framework benefits
sections.summary: The new regulatory framework will enhance food safety enforcement, support the local agri-food sector and bolster food security against supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new regulatory framework will enhance our capabilities for food safety enforcement, support the growth of our local agri-food sector and bolster food security against potential supply disruptions caused by outbreaks, climate change or global conflicts.

sections.label: Preventive measures in new Bill
sections.summary: The passage asks what preventive measures the new Bill will introduce, beyond enforcement and increased penalties, to mitigate future lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Beyond enforcement and increased penalties, what preventive measures will the new Bill introduce to mitigate future lapses?

sections.label: Assistance schemes and training decriminalisation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will introduce assistance schemes for businesses and expresses concern about decriminalising food workers' training failures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry introduce assistance schemes – such as grants, access to financing schemes or insurance programmes – to help these businesses recover swiftly and stay operational? : I am also concerned about the proposal to decriminalise failures by food workers to attend training.

sections.label: Food import limit and biosecurity risks
sections.summary: The new 15 kilogrammes limit on food imports for private consumption will delight some residents, but carries correlated risks of heightened biosecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the new limit of 15 kilogrammes on food imports for private consumption will delight some residents, there are correlated risks of heightened biosecurity threats.

sections.label: Food businesses' core obligations
sections.summary: The Bill establishes food-related businesses' core obligations and responsibilities to workers, consumers, and other agri-food supply chain businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill establishes food-related businesses' core obligations and responsibilities to workers, consumers, and other businesses in the agri-food supply chain.

sections.label: F&B business closures 2024
sections.summary: The Business Times reported close to 2,500 F&B businesses ceased operations in the first nine months of 2024, a 19.7% increase over 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Business Times reported that close to 2,500 F&B businesses ceased operations in the first nine months of 2024, representing an increase of 19.7% over the whole of 2023.

sections.label: License applicant knowledge and contraventions
sections.summary: Sub-section 4b requires license applicants to have relevant knowledge, competency and experience, and asks if SFA considers past employment contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sub-section 4b states that a license applicant must have, “relevant knowledge, competency and experience in identifying, controlling, managing and eliminating or minimising hazards for the purpose of achieving safe and suitable food in carrying on that licensable food business.” To this end, could the Minister share if SFA takes into consideration past employment contraventions of license applicants when assessing these applicants' suitability to operate food businesses?

sections.label: Minimum stockpile requirements
sections.summary: SFA is considering requiring key food operators and farm feed suppliers other than white rice to meet minimum stockpile requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In order to strengthen our country's food security, in addition to the MSR that white rice importers must comply with under the current rice reserve program, SFA is considering requiring key food operators and farm feed suppliers other than for white rice to meet minimum stockpile requirements in the future.

sections.label: Home-based food business exception
sections.summary: The only exception would be home-based food businesses, which fall outside current licensing requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The only exception would be home-based food businesses which fall outside current licensing requirements.

sections.label: Tracking home-based food businesses
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister would consider tracking home-based food businesses and clarify operating one in a second premise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider some simple form of tracking the number of home-based food businesses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister also clarify, whether an operator can establish a home-based food business in a second premise whether this is an owned or rented property?

sections.label: Assistance for producers transitioning
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister whether further assistance will be considered for producers transitioning toward a sustainable business level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we will need to bridge this phase together, could the Minister kindly update us whether there will be further assistance considered for the producers as they transition toward a sustainable business level?

sections.label: Novel food pre-market approval
sections.summary: Companies unsure if a food is novel should consult SFA, and those supplying novel food must seek pre-market approval with a safety assessment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When in doubt on whether a food or food ingredient is considered a novel food in the first place, companies should consult SFA to discuss the available evidence on the history of safe use that they have compiled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Companies that intend to supply novel food are required to seek SFA's pre-market approval.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To obtain pre-market approval, companies must conduct and submit safety assessment of the novel food for SFA's review.

sections.label: Unlicensed food business activities prohibited
sections.summary: Clause 104 prohibits an unlicensed food business from undertaking certain activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In addition, clause 104 prohibits an unlicensed food business from undertaking certain activities.

sections.label: Directions to food workers
sections.summary: Clause 130 allows the DG (FA) to issue directions directly to a food worker where a food safety lapse is due entirely to the worker.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That said, we agree that food workers also have a responsibility in ensuring food safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I want to assure Mr Don Wee that even while we are decriminalising failure by food worker to attend food handling training, clause 130 will allow the DG (FA), in appropriate cases, to issue directions directly to the food worker to enable targeted interventions where the food safety lapse is due entirely to the worker.

sections.label: Community garden licensing exemption considerations
sections.summary: SFA's main consideration in regulating primary production is minimising human health risks from agri-food inputs, and 200 kilogrammes monthly or less is considered small scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Ms Carrie Tan gave the example of chickens being used in farms to help till soil and provide organic fertiliser, and asked about the considerations behind exempting licensing for community gardens only when their monthly production volume is less than 200 kilogrammes and there is no use of human excreta, or raw animal or bird excreta as manure, as well as pesticides, during the cultivation process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SFA's principal consideration in regulating primary production activity is to minimise the risks to human health from agri-food production inputs including fertilisers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We consider a monthly production volume of 200 kilogrammes per month or less as small scale, which limits the extent of the potential food safety impact.

sections.label: Limit on non-commercial poultry
sections.summary: Under the Animals and Birds Rules, no person shall keep more than 10 non-commercial poultry in any premise to mitigate avian disease spread.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In accordance with the Animals and Birds (Prevention of Avian Disease in Non-commercial Poultry) Rules, no person shall keep more than 10 non-commercial poultry in any premise to mitigate the risk of spread of avian disease and to safeguard human and animal health.

sections.label: Extending stockpiling to food items
sections.summary: Essential food items or agri-food inputs may be subject to stockpiling requirements if needed, with no immediate plans beyond rice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This will enable us to subject essential food items or agri-food production inputs to stockpiling requirements, if the need arises in the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And as I had shared earlier, there are no immediate plans to extend MSR to entities other than rice importers, or to commodities beyond rice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If there is a need to extend MSR to other food items or agri-food production inputs, we will engage the relevant stakeholders before doing so and give MSR entities sufficient lead time to comply with the requirements.

sections.label: Reviewing food supply resilience
sections.summary: The Government will regularly review food supply resilience, and farms are not constrained by prescriptive food safety requirements in primary production.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government will review our food supply resilience situation regularly to ensure a careful balance between how we deploy MSR to meet our national food security needs and the potential costs to the industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under the new approach, as proposed under the Bill, farms are not constrained by prescriptive requirements to ensure food safety in their primary production activity.

sections.label: Consultation numbers on food bill
sections.summary: 1,500 companies, associations and entities were consulted, with feedback from 112 respondents and 260 in-person participants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: A total of 1,500 companies, associations and entities have been consulted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: MSE and SFA received feedback from 112 respondents via REACH and 260 participants who attended the in-person engagement sessions.

sections.label: Amended novel food definition
sections.summary: The novel food definition was amended to exclude food additives and to state that mineral-origin material like rock salt is not novel food.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, we amended the definition of novel food for clarity by excluding food additives; and including a qualifier that material of mineral origin, such as rock salt, will not be considered novel food.

sections.label: Food Control Plans for businesses
sections.summary: Some licensed food businesses must have a Food Control Plan, with fewer and simpler components for smaller-scale operations than larger ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, some licensed food businesses will be required to have a Food Control Plan and the components of the plan for smaller-scale operations would be much fewer and simpler than that for larger-scale operations like food caterers.

sections.label: Bill foundation for food supply
sections.summary: Regulations can promote industry development, and the Bill provides a foundation for a safe and secure food supply in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Regulations can provide greater clarity, assurance and public trust, which can, in turn, promote industry development and build an innovative ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic and recent geopolitical tensions have laid bare the fragility of global food supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This Bill provides a solid foundation for all stakeholders to continue to work together towards a safe and secure food supply in Singapore.

sections.label: Outdated food deemed unsuitable
sections.summary: The Bill treats "outdated" food as "unsuitable" and bans its supply, with "outdated" defined by date marking in Subsidiary Legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Under the Bill, "outdated" food will be considered "unsuitable" food, the supply of which will not be permitted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The meaning of what constitutes "outdated" relates to date marking requirements and will be prescribed by Subsidiary Legislation.

sections.label: Good Samaritan defences available
sections.summary: Clause 164 states the defences in the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act are available against offences in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Clause 164 explicitly states that the defences in the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act are available against offences in the Bill.

sections.label: Private consumption allowance restrictions
sections.summary: Clause 160 makes clear food brought in under the private consumption allowance cannot be sold or donated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Clause 160 makes clear that any food brought in under the private consumption allowance cannot be sold or donated.

sections.label: SFA inspection scheme powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives SFA powers to establish inspection schemes, identify items needing prior import clearance, and set inspection levels for hazards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Bill will provide powers for SFA to establish inspection schemes, to identify food and other controlled items which require prior clearance for import, what is needed for this clearance, and the different levels of inspection for specific hazards.

sections.label: Maximum fine quantum reference
sections.summary: The $50,000 maximum fine takes reference from the Wholesome Meat and Fish Act, which already provides that maximum for selling unfit meat or fish.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The maximum fine quantum of $50,000 takes reference from the Wholesome Meat and Fish Act, which today already provides for a maximum fine of $50,000 for offenders who sell meat or fish that is unfit for human consumption.

sections.label: Regulatory action for defaults
sections.summary: These defaults form a ground for SFA regulatory action, ranging from suspension or cancellation of licence to a financial penalty of up to $5,000 per contravention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Specifically, any of these defaults will form a ground for regulatory action by SFA, which can range from suspension or cancelling the licence to imposing a financial penalty of up to $5,000 per contravention.

sections.label: Food safety bill aims
sections.summary: The Bill aims to strengthen food safety, reduce regulatory complexity, cut compliance cost, support industry growth, and enable responses to food safety and security threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Bill will strengthen food safety to better protect consumers; reduce regulatory complexity, thereby increasing ease of doing business, reducing compliance cost, and supporting industry innovation and growth; and enable effective responses to food safety and security threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Ultimately, safe and secure food is existential; it is essential to the normal functioning of our daily lives, our economy, our security, our entire society.

sections.label: Citation year change
sections.summary: The citation year "2024" will be changed to "2025" as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2024" will be changed to "2025" as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
